title: Minimax Estimation of Conditional Squared Wasserstein Distance near Equality and Boundary Degeneracy
banked_reason: Final D0.5 math and decision reviews pass, but the sound unmatched conditional frontier and calibration result scores subfield 6.8 below the field cutoff 7 after both reroutes.
gap_reasons: For d≥1, the central minimax theorem proves an intrinsic lower frontier but only a strictly slower observable upper envelope, so it does not determine the quadratic-zone rate.
The growing-rank transition applies only to an infeasible population-score, population-kernel statistic, while the load-bearing observable mixed-regime calibration remains open.
The isotropic transfer is likewise an unmatched bracket on a class constructed in the note rather than a resolution of the published SmoothCOT class.
proof_attempt_summary: The run repaired the anisotropic cross-term proof, the false two-sided linear-variance equivalence, the Gateaux-direction domain, and the d=0 projector centering, then proved an honest unmatched bracket on both the native class and a fixed-radius positive-isotropic scalar SmoothCOT slice. The d≥1 observable upper rates remain polynomially slower than the intrinsic quadratic lower rate, and the population Gaussian–quadratic transition does not yield an observable all-regime interval. Reaching field tier now requires genuinely new estimator, relative spectral/Hessian, multiplier-coupling, and anti-concentration machinery.
tldr: For \(d\ge1\), conditional squared Wasserstein distance has an anisotropic boundary geometry: inverse ellipticity smooths outcome frequencies while covariate resolution replicates the ordered spectrum. The sign-paired family supplies the zero and quadratic lower components, while a separate fixed-frequency, constant-in-\(z\) two-point family supplies the regular \(\rho n^{-1/2}\) component; together they yield the intrinsic lower frontier \(\min\{\rho^2,\rho n^{-1/2}+n^{-4s_z/(4s_z+d)}\}\), while the zero estimator, the explicit Gram-corrected estimator, median SmoothCOT, and, when available, median direct-COT give a computable observable upper envelope; the nontrivial quadratic zone remains an honest unmatched bracket. Under the theorem's stated triangular conditions, the infeasible oracle-score, population-kernel statistic has Gaussian limits for \(d\ge1\); no observable-experiment Gaussianization or calibration is claimed. The separate \(d=0\) branch recovers the two-sample del Barrio--Gin\'e--Utzet law and \(n^{-1}\) scale. Uniform mixed-regime calibration remains open.
gap: SmoothCOT Section 3.3, Theorem 3.2, Remark 3.2, and Appendix C.4 stop at a regular CLT and faster-than-root-\(n\) equality statement. Existing unconditional Wasserstein laws, changing-kernel theory, fixed-entropic causal transport, and the direct-estimation COT abstract do not provide a verified observable equality-local anisotropic frontier.
fill: The project derives canonical ordered-spectrum and bias bounds, constructs the foldwise clipped ridge-Galerkin statistic, states the normalized triangular experiment and regular studentization with exact split constants, matches the pilot-feasible rate using a checked sign-paired wavelet family, and isolates honest all-regime calibration as the unresolved node.
